summary: This memo gives IESG advice arising from reviewing Path MTU Discovery for advancement. It found that some routers optionally suppress ICMP messages, which breaks the mechanism, and outlines a change to that practice. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: Path MTU Discovery depends on a router reporting when a packet is too large for a link. RFC 1435 advises routers to keep sending that specific ICMP message even when they suppress other ICMP messages.

subtitle: IESG advice on which ICMP message routers should still send when ICMP suppression is enabled.

tldr.problem: Some routers can suppress ICMP messages to avoid problems with older BSD hosts. That can make Path MTU Discovery fail without a clear signal to the sender.
tldr.mechanism: The memo advises routers to continue sending ICMP Type 3 code 4 when the Don't Fragment bit is set and fragmentation is required, even if general ICMP suppression is enabled.
tldr.outcome: This advice is intended to let Path MTU Discovery work while leaving older BSD hosts unaffected, since the memo says they do not set the DF bit.

facts.label: Condition
facts.value: DF bit set and fragmentation required

today: RFC 1435 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata lists no RFC as obsoleting or updating it. It gives advice on router behavior and does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: Why ICMP Suppression Causes a Problem
sections.content:
While reviewing Path MTU Discovery for possible advancement to Draft Standard, the IESG learned that some routers could be configured to disable ICMP messages generated by the router. The reported reason was to protect older BSD hosts, which could drop all connections to a host after receiving an ICMP message on any connection, even a non-fatal message.

The memo says this suppression can make Path MTU Discovery fail silently and make the failure hard to diagnose. Without the router's message, the sender does not learn that a packet needs to be smaller for part of its path.
sections.plainLanguage: Some routers suppress ICMP messages to avoid problems with older BSD hosts. But Path MTU Discovery needs a router to report when a packet is too large.

sections.title: The ICMP Message to Keep Sending
sections.content:
The IESG advice is to keep sending ICMP Type 3 code 4, meaning destination unreachable because fragmentation is required while the Don't Fragment (DF) bit is set. Routers should send this message even when their “don't send ICMP messages” switch is enabled.

The memo says this should allow Path MTU Discovery to work without affecting the older BSD hosts described above, because those hosts never set the DF bit in their packets.
sections.plainLanguage: Even with general ICMP suppression enabled, a router should report that a packet with DF set is too large to forward without fragmentation. The memo says older BSD hosts are unaffected because they do not set DF.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo states that security issues are not discussed. Its subject is router behavior needed for Path MTU Discovery.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo does not discuss security. It focuses on keeping a specific router message available to Path MTU Discovery.
